source_text: Ita natura praescripsit esse quaedam, quae ut ratio, ita fides cum religione pronuntiet; et tamen pudor et decentia conversationis oculis non permittat exponi. Hoc modo Magister etiam Gentium veritatem carni eius assignat, et spiritui sanctitatem. Magnum, inquit, pietatis sacramentum, quod manifestatum est in carne, iustificatum est in spiritu, apparuit Angelis, praedicatum est in Gentibus, creditum est in hoc mundo, assumptum est in gloria [n87] . Quod sicut commendavit cum veritate credendum, ita impugnatores eius in fine denuntiavit saeculi nascituros; nam statim sequitur: In novissimis autem temporibus recedent quidam a fide, attendentes spiritibus seductoribus, doctrinis daemoniorum in hypocrisi mendacia loquentium, cauteriatam habentes conscientiam, prohibentium nubere, abstinere a cibis, quos Deus creavit ad percipiendum cum gratiarum actione fidelibus, et his qui cognoverunt veritatem; quoniam omnis creatura Dei bona [n88] . Hanc ergo Ecclesiarum contaminationem, quam de Manichaei consectatione vomuisti, et hanc a fide recedentium praevaricationem, quae in naturalis mali praedicatione et in commixtionis coniugalis damnatione consistit, et Apostolus praevidit et punivit, non solum quid diceretur, sed etiam quid consequeretur ostendens.
pass_a_gloss: Thus nature prescribed that there are certain things which, as reason, so faith with religion may pronounce; and nevertheless modesty and the becomingness of the way of life may not permit them to be set out before the eyes. In this manner the Teacher of the Nations also assigns truth to his flesh, and holiness to the spirit. Great, he says, is the sacrament of piety, which was manifested in the flesh, was justified in the spirit, appeared to Angels, was preached among the Nations, was believed in this world, was taken up in glory. Which as he commended as to be believed with truth, so he denounced that its attackers would be born at the end of the age; for immediately it follows: But in the last times some will recede from the faith, attending to seducing spirits, to doctrines of demons speaking lies in hypocrisy, having a cauterized conscience, forbidding to marry, to abstain from foods which God created for receiving with thanksgiving by the faithful, and by those who have known the truth; because every creature of God is good. This contamination of the Churches therefore, which you vomited from the following of Manichaeus, and this prevarication of those receding from the faith, which consists in the preaching of natural evil and in the condemnation of marital mingling, both the Apostle foresaw and punished, showing not only what would be said, but also what would follow.

pass_b_english: Thus nature has prescribed that there are certain things reason, and likewise faith with reverence, may name, though modesty and decency of conduct do not allow them to be exposed to sight. In this way the Teacher of the Nations assigns reality to Christ’s flesh and holiness to his spirit: “Great,” he says, “is the mystery of devotion, which was manifested in flesh, justified in spirit, appeared to angels, was preached among the nations, was believed in this world, and was taken up in glory” (1 Timothy 3:16). Just as he commended this to be believed as true, so he announced that its opponents would arise at the end of the age. For he immediately continues: “In the last times some will depart from the faith, attending to deceitful spirits and teachings of demons, speaking lies in hypocrisy, having their conscience seared, forbidding marriage, requiring abstinence from foods that God created to be received with thanksgiving by the faithful and by those who have known the truth; for every creature of God is good” (1 Timothy 4:1–4).

The apostle both foresaw and condemned this pollution of the churches that you vomited out by following Manichaeus: this betrayal by those departing from the faith, which consists in preaching natural evil and condemning marital union. He showed not only what would be said, but also what would follow from it.

choices.why: Julian defends marital union (commixtio) as God's work, not the devil's property.
Julian's Manichaean charge: an evil that is a nature, not a will's act.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
